decks.title: The Forgiving Fortress
decks.objective: The slot that has to survive turns 1-5 against a fast start, then convert everything it accumulated into a decisive finish. This is the deck you learn combat math on, so it should punish very few mistakes and reward patience.

decks.title: The Long Game
decks.objective: The high-ceiling slot — the deck you grow into over months. It should reward reading the table, answering only what genuinely needs answering, and out-lasting three opponents through accumulated advantage rather than a single explosive turn.

decks.title: The City Builder
decks.objective: The literal infrastructure deck — lands as the city. It should feel like every single turn advances the board, reward patience with compounding returns, and eventually produce an overwhelming position rather than a sudden kill.

decks.title: The Reactive Engine
decks.objective: The slot that reads three opponents and responds intelligently. It should hold the fort with cheap answers, accrue value passively while doing so, and eventually reach a position where the accumulated engine simply wins.

decks.title: The Immediate Engine
decks.objective: The fast-rhythm slot — something happens every turn from turn four onward. It should be the deck you reach for when you want action rather than patience, while still surviving a wipe.

decks.title: The Capstone
decks.objective: The flagship — the deck that out-resources three opponents and can win from behind. It should reward the most decisions per turn and be the one you graduate into once the other five feel automatic.

Base Variant · Deck 1
Claude’s Choice

Ancestral Bulwark — Betor

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Betor, Ancestor's Voice{3}{W}{B}{G} Legendary Creature — Spirit DragonFlying, lifelink. At your end step, put +1/+1 counters on a creature equal to life gained this turn, and reanimate a creature with mana value ≤ life lost.$3.61

Deck rarity — by stage

Base65%Fairly familiar
Tuned69%Uncommon
Maxed73%Uncommon

Modelled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (5396 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognise.

Precon seed

Abzan Armor Tarkir: Dragonstorm 2025 In print ~$45 $82 total
Why this commander

Two triggers in one end step, and they feed each other: life you gained becomes +1/+1 counters, life you lost reanimates a creature. Most commanders make you choose between growing and rebuilding. Betor does both off the same combat, without spending a card.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Soul Warden{W}Creature — Human ClericGain 1 life whenever any other creature enters — yours or theirs. Fires on everyone's turn, not just yours.$3.14
Authority of the Consuls{W}EnchantmentOpponents' creatures enter tapped AND you gain 1 life each. Blunts a rush and feeds Betor off the same card.$4.72
Pristine Talisman{3}ArtifactTaps for mana and gains 1 life. Guaranteed lifegain every single turn with zero setup — this is the card that makes the trigger reliable.$0.34
Trelasarra, Moon Dancer{G}{W}Legendary Creature — Elf ClericEvery lifegain event is a +1/+1 counter and a scry. A second Betor for two mana.$0.26
Dawn of Hope{1}{W}EnchantmentTurns lifegain into cards, and builds lifelink blockers with spare mana.$0.47
Blood Artist{1}{B}Creature — VampireDrains on every death anywhere — and it can target YOU: one death then feeds both halves of Betor at once.$3.09
Branching Evolution{2}{G}EnchantmentDoubles every +1/+1 counter you would place.$6.43
Well of Lost Dreams{4}ArtifactTurns your lifegain into cards.$0.99
Inspiring Call{2}{G}InstantDraw per counter-creature and make them indestructible — the only wipe answer.$0.20

How it plays

KEITH1Ramp behind walls, land Betor, then attack into damage on purpose so the lifegain converts to counters at end step. It runs almost on autopilot, which is exactly why it is forgiving — and exactly why it plateaus once you know the loop.

  • Fortress: best in the lineup — nothing attacks profitably into it.
  • Convergence: weak. Counters are additive, not combinatorial.
  • Wipes: one Inspiring Call is the entire insurance policy.

What Keith said

I don't see enough life gain in this deck to reliably trigger your commander. It's on a few creatures and your commander, and your commander can land a hit and trigger it, but having to attack with your commander is risky. I'd add more non-combat lifegain.
Good call — taken in full
  • Added six non-combat lifegain sources. Soul Warden, Authority of the Consuls, Pristine Talisman, Trelasarra, Dawn of Hope and Blood Artist. None of them require an attack, and three of them fire on opponents' turns.
  • Betor no longer has to swing. Pristine Talisman alone guarantees lifegain every turn just by tapping for mana, so the end-step trigger is live whether or not you go to combat.
  • Cut the counter redundancy that was doing nothing. Karn's Bastion, Contagion Clasp, Nesting Grounds, Evolution Sage and Conclave Mentor came out to pay for it — you had plenty of ways to multiply counters and almost no way to make the first one.
  • The road past Tuned leans into Betor's other half. The Maxed route now leads with Necropotence — paying life IS 'life lost this turn', which switches on the reanimation clause while refilling your hand — and Phyrexian Arena heads the ladder for the same reason.
  • Net cost +$7.27. $74.73 to $82.00.

Room to grow — what this framework supports later

Headroom34 cards
Upgrade value~$12 ea

The two dot rows score 34 cards costing about $411 in total — roughly $12 a card, or 8.3 upgrades per $100. That total is the 9 upgrades listed above, plus about 22 more archetype-specific cards on the advanced ladder (~$245), plus the three Game Changers below (~$146). Headroom is how long that whole ladder is; Upgrade value is how cheaply it climbs.

The next cards you would buy
  • Phyrexian Arena
  • The Ozolith
  • Innkeeper's Talent
  • Vorinclex, Monstrous Raider
  • Doubling Season

Where it sits on the Bracket 2 – 3 line

Bracket 2
Core2.57Bracket 3
Upgraded
High Bracket 2 · 0 of 3 Game Changers used

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modelled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
Route to the top of Bracket 3 — three colour-legal Game Changers, about $146
Game Changer$What it buys you
Necropotence$36Trades life for a fistful of cards - a fortress can afford the life.
Teferi's Protection$48Your whole board and life total phase out - the single best answer to a wipe, and it hits nobody else.
Smothering Tithe$62Every opponent draw either pays you or taxes them. Pure ramp, no targets.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are picked from the current 53-card Game Changers roster (Farewell and Biorhythm added 9 Feb 2026), filtered to this commander’s colour identity, ordered by how well they serve a defensive build-up seat, and skipping reserved-list trophies over $130. Prices are live Scryfall market prices as of 21 Aug 2026.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Value lives on creatures as counters — the most wipe-fragile storage in Magic. Two removal spells in 100 cards cannot answer a growing threat across the table.
Claude’s Choice

The fixes changed this ranking. Before the lifegain rework this build could not reliably trigger its own commander; now six non-combat sources fire every turn, Blood Artist can point at you to switch on BOTH halves, and the Maxed route through Necropotence feeds the reanimation clause directly. It keeps the box and plan you already own, sits at $82 against a $110 brief, and scores 5/5 Fortress and Friendly. The best version of the deck you were already buying.

Why this commander

A one-card loop. Saprolings die, every opponent loses life, you gain it, and you can pay to kill your own tokens whenever you like. A board wipe stops being a disaster and becomes a stack of drain triggers.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$

Tendershoot Dryad{4}{G}Creature — DryadA Saproling every upkeep — yours AND theirs — that grows the whole tribe. The city-builder this list was missing.$1.04
Fungal Plots{1}{G}EnchantmentGraveyard creatures become Saprolings; spare Saprolings become cards. Quiet, engine-shaped value.$0.25
Dictate of Erebos{3}{B}{B}EnchantmentYour creature dies, everyone sacrifices. Beats big-creature decks. Stretch.$16.60

You never need to attack. Fodder plus a sacrifice outlet plus a drain enchantment are three unrelated cards that together end the game — genuinely convergent. The catch against your profile: it has no real early defence, so a rush deck can pressure you before the pieces assemble.

Rebuild option · Deck 1
Claude’s Runner-up

Abzan Toughness Fortress — Felothar

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Felothar the Steadfast{1}{W}{B}{G} Legendary Creature — Human WarriorYour creatures deal combat damage using toughness instead of power, defenders may attack, and Felothar can turn a spare creature into new cards.in box

Deck rarity — by stage

Base83%Rarely seen
Tuned87%Rarely seen
Maxed89%Rarely seen

Modelled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (5258 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognise.

Precon seed

Abzan Armor Tarkir: Dragonstorm 2025 In print ~$45 $50 total
Why this commander

Felothar puts the whole plan in the command zone: your walls deal damage with toughness, defenders can attack, and a spare high-toughness creature can be exchanged for a new hand. The defensive board becomes an attack without waiting to draw a separate enabler.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Assault Formation{1}{G}EnchantmentA backup copy of Felothar's toughness-damage effect in case the commander is removed. In the box.in box
Huatli, the Sun's Heart{2}{G/W}Legendary PlaneswalkerThird copy of the toughness-damage effect, on a permanent wipes don't hit.$0.43
Wall of Omens{1}{W}Creature — WallA blocker that replaces itself. The template for the whole deck.$0.31
Vindicate{1}{W}{B}SorceryDestroy any permanent — the removal the original lacked.$0.67
Anguished Unmaking{1}{W}{B}InstantExile any nonland permanent, answering indestructible threats.$1.42
Unbreakable Formation{2}{W}InstantYour board becomes indestructible — real wipe insurance.$1.42
Sun Titan{4}{W}{W}Creature — GiantRebuys a fallen permanent on every attack.$0.38

How it plays

This is the purest expression of 'defend while I build, then swing big'. Every wall you play is a brick in the city and a future attacker; the turn Felothar lands, a board everyone had written off as passive becomes lethal. Treefolk and living fortifications also give it a real narrative ode.

  • One-card setup: Felothar supplies both toughness-based damage and permission for defenders to attack.

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modelled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
Route to the top of Bracket 3 — three colour-legal Game Changers, about $138
Game Changer$What it buys you
Teferi's Protection$48Your whole board and life total phase out - the single best answer to a wipe, and it hits nobody else.
Aura Shards$29Every creature you land becomes free artifact/enchantment removal.
Smothering Tithe$62Every opponent draw either pays you or taxes them. Pure ramp, no targets.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are picked from the current 53-card Game Changers roster (Farewell and Biorhythm added 9 Feb 2026), filtered to this commander’s colour identity, ordered by how well they serve a defensive build-up seat, and skipping reserved-list trophies over $130. Prices are live Scryfall market prices as of 21 Aug 2026.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Still a creature-board deck, so protect the wall before committing every defender. Felothar's card filtering improves recovery, but Unbreakable Formation and Sun Titan remain important.
Claude’s Runner-up

The real challenger to Betor: Felothar supplies the attack conversion, defender permission, and card filtering from the command zone while already sitting in the sealed deck. Betor remains first for the lifegain-and-reanimation ceiling; Felothar is now close enough to overtake it if reliable wall combat and simpler setup matter more than that ceiling.

Precon seed

Any Orzhov lifegain box, or singles e.g. Wilds of Eldraine / Duskmourn shells Flexible seed ~$30 $80 total
Why this commander

Taxes every opponent's spell by two life and hands the life to you, passively, without ever targeting anyone. Next to lifelink blockers it turns your life total from a buffer into the deck's actual fuel.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Sanguine Bond{3}{B}{B}EnchantmentWhenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much.$5.98
Marauding Blight-Priest{2}{B}Creature — Vampire ClericA second Sanguine Bond on a body, for thirty cents. No loop, all redundancy.$0.30
Epicure of Blood{4}{B}Creature — VampireA third copy of the drain effect. The engine no longer lives on one enchantment.$0.31
Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose{2}{B}{B}Creature — Vampire ClericA creature-shaped Sanguine Bond — a second half to the combo.$10.74
Aetherflux Reservoir{4}ArtifactPay 50 life: deal 50 damage to any target. A third, independent convergence line.$20.12
Lyra Dawnbringer{3}{W}{W}Legendary Creature — Angel5/5 flying, first strike, lifelink; pumps your other Angels. Defence and clock in one.$0.46
Felidar Sovereign{4}{W}{W}Creature — Cat BeastAt upkeep, if you're at 40+ life, you win the game. A fourth win route.$1.96
Crested Sunmare{3}{W}{W}Creature — HorseAn indestructible 5/5 Horse every turn you gained life — a wipe-proof army.$8.89

How it plays

This is the deck your rant described. You spend the early game as the least attractive target at the table — lifelinking angels and horses, life total climbing, nobody profits from hitting you. Meanwhile you are quietly assembling four independent win routes: Sanguine Bond + Exquisite Blood, Vito + any lifegain, Aetherflux Reservoir, and Felidar Sovereign. Any two halves meeting ends the game across all three opponents simultaneously, and until that moment you look like the harmless lifegain player.

Profile-tuned · Deck 1
Claude’s 4th Place

Abzan Fungus Engine — Ghave

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Ghave, Guru of Spores{2}{B}{G}{W} Legendary Creature — Fungus Shaman{1}, remove a +1/+1 counter from a creature: make a 1/1 Saproling. Sacrifice a creature: put a +1/+1 counter on target creature.$1.06

Deck rarity — by stage

Base89%Rarely seen
Tuned91%Almost never seen
Maxed93%Almost never seen

Modelled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (9633 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognise.

Precon seed

Abzan Armor Tarkir: Dragonstorm 2025 In print ~$45 $79 total
Why this commander

The most flexible counter commander printed: creatures into counters, counters back into creatures, at instant speed, for free. That loop is the seed of half of Abzan's combos, which is why its upgrade ladder never runs out.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Ashnod's Altar{3}ArtifactSacrifice a creature for {C}{C}. With Ghave this becomes a loop that makes as many Saprolings as you have mana.$14.97
Blood Artist{1}{B}Creature — VampireTurns the loop into damage across all three opponents.$3.09
Cathars' Crusade{3}{W}{W}EnchantmentEvery token entering pumps the whole board — the go-wide payoff.$9.46
Mazirek, Kraul Death Priest{3}{B}{G}Legendary Creature — Insect ShamanEvery sacrifice grows the whole team.$0.35
Second Harvest{2}{G}{G}InstantDoubles your entire token board at instant speed.$5.14

How it plays

Ghave is a two-way converter, which is exactly the 'pieces that suddenly connect' shape. Early it just makes chump blockers and grows your board — completely unthreatening. Later, Ghave plus a free sacrifice outlet plus any drain effect is three unrelated cards that together end the game. It is the most engine-like Deck 1 option and it uses the box you were already buying.

  • Convergence: among the highest here — three commonly-drawn pieces form a real engine.
  • Build-up: counters and tokens are the same resource, so nothing you invest is wasted.
  • Resilience: the commander rebuilds the board from any single counter.

Room to grow — what this framework supports later

Upgrade value~$15 ea

The two dot rows score 34 cards costing about $511 in total — roughly $15 a card, or 6.7 upgrades per $100. That total is the 5 upgrades listed above, plus about 26 more archetype-specific cards on the advanced ladder (~$340), plus the three Game Changers below (~$138). Headroom is how long that whole ladder is; Upgrade value is how cheaply it climbs.

Where it sits on the Bracket 2 – 3 line

Core2.64Bracket 3
Upgraded

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modelled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
Route to the top of Bracket 3 — three colour-legal Game Changers, about $138
Game Changer$What it buys you
Aura Shards$29Every creature you land becomes free artifact/enchantment removal.
Teferi's Protection$48Your whole board and life total phase out - the single best answer to a wipe, and it hits nobody else.
Smothering Tithe$62Every opponent draw either pays you or taxes them. Pure ramp, no targets.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are picked from the current 53-card Game Changers roster (Farewell and Biorhythm added 9 Feb 2026), filtered to this commander’s colour identity, ordered by how well they serve a defensive build-up seat, and skipping reserved-list trophies over $130. Prices are live Scryfall market prices as of 21 Aug 2026.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Ashnod's Altar at $15 is the piece that turns it from 'good value deck' into 'engine'. Without a free sac outlet it is noticeably slower.
Claude’s 4th Place

Fourth, displaced by the repaired Liesa build rather than by any fault of its own. The counters-into-bodies engine is still exactly the pieces-that-connect shape, and it keeps the longest ladder in the row. It stays behind 1c because 51% assembly and a $15 Ashnod's Altar dependency are structural, while 1c's two disqualifiers were removable — and were removed.

Base Variant · Deck 2
Claude’s 3rd Place

The Withering — The Reaper

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
The Reaper, King No More{2/B}{2/R}{2/G} Legendary Artifact Creature — ScarecrowETB: a -1/-1 counter on up to two creatures. Whenever an opponent's creature with a -1/-1 counter on it dies, you may put that card onto the battlefield under your control — once each turn. That is once each TURN, not each round: with deaths on other players' turns it can fire up to four times a rotation.$0.45

Deck rarity — by stage

Base66%Fairly familiar
Tuned70%Uncommon
Maxed74%Uncommon

Modelled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (6085 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognise.

Precon seed

Blight Curse Lorwyn Eclipsed In print ~$28 $42 total
Why this commander

Turns removal into permanent shrinkage instead of a one-shot answer. -1/-1 counters stay put, so every small hit compounds across turns rather than resetting.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Necroskitter{1}{B}{B}Creature — ElementalA second Reaper with no once-per-turn clause: every opponent creature that dies holding a -1/-1 counter comes back under your control.$0.39
Hapatra, Vizier of Poisons{B}{G}Legendary Creature — Human ClericEvery -1/-1 counter you place also makes a 1/1 deathtouch Snake. Legal here because The Reaper is Jund, not Rakdos.$0.29
Kulrath Knight{3}{B/R}{B/R}Creature — Elemental KnightAnything holding a counter can't attack or block. The defensive piece the deck was missing.$0.23
Ichor Rats{1}{B}{B}Creature — Phyrexian RatThe card Keith called out. Infect: its damage IS -1/-1 counters, feeding every engine here.$2.06
Throne of Geth{1}ArtifactSacrifice an artifact: proliferate. The deck's one real sacrifice outlet.$1.02
Nest of Scarabs{2}{B}EnchantmentEvery -1/-1 counter also makes a 1/1 Insect.$3.99
Grim Affliction{2}{B}SorceryOne counter, then proliferate.$0.32
Serrated Arrows{4}ArtifactThree counters over three turns.$0.25

How it plays

Mark a threat, let it die, take it. The fantasy is excellent and the execution is a power tier short — your removal is sized for 2/2s in a pod full of 7/7s.

Assembly56%
  • Friendly: low. Taking opponents' creatures is the highest-salt thing in the lineup.
  • Fortress: poor — you have no way to not-die while setting up.

What Keith said

Probably my favorite deck, this effect is so rare and stealing cards is a blast. Seems to be tons of synergy in the deck already. Ichor Rats is a great upgrade. Bloodbriar... are you sacrificing creatures? I don't think so...
Good call — taken in full
  • Bloodbriar is out. He was right — the only things this deck ever sacrifices are Throne of Geth eating an artifact and Nihil Spellbomb cashing itself in, so Bloodbriar was a vanilla 2/3 for three. Worse, it wants +1/+1 counters in a deck that deals exclusively in -1/-1 counters.
  • Necroskitter in its place. It is a second copy of the effect Keith likes, with no once-per-turn clause: any opponent creature that dies with a -1/-1 counter comes back under your control.
  • Blowfly Infestation was considered — and deliberately shelved. With Hapatra or Nest of Scarabs it is a true two-card infinite loop: a 1/1 token dies holding a counter, Blowfly re-places the counter, the replacement token dies, forever. Bracket 2 allows no two-card infinite combos, so Blowfly waits at the top of the advanced ladder as the Maxed-stage finisher, clearly labelled.
  • Hapatra and Kulrath Knight added. Hapatra turns each counter into a deathtouch Snake; Kulrath Knight stops anything holding a counter from attacking or blocking, which fixes the defensive hole.
  • Corrected the commander line. The Reaper costs {2/B}{2/R}{2/G} and its colour identity is Jund, not Rakdos — the page had it wrong, which also means Golgari cards like Hapatra are legal here.
  • Net cost +$0.87. $41.20 to $42.07 — and Keith's Ichor Rats is now a headline card instead of a footnote.

Room to grow — what this framework supports later

Headroom25 cards
Upgrade value~$12 ea

The two dot rows score 25 cards costing about $297 in total — roughly $12 a card, or 8.4 upgrades per $100. That total is the 8 upgrades listed above, plus about 14 more archetype-specific cards on the advanced ladder (~$165), plus the three Game Changers below (~$123). Headroom is how long that whole ladder is; Upgrade value is how cheaply it climbs.

The next cards you would buy

  • Grim Poppet
  • Midnight Reaper
  • Black Market Connections
  • Archfiend of Ifnir

Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modelled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
Route to the top of Bracket 3 — three colour-legal Game Changers, about $123
Game Changer$What it buys you
Necropotence$36Trades life for a fistful of cards - a fortress can afford the life.
Orcish Bowmasters$46Instant-speed value that punishes extra draws.
Jeska's Will$41A burst of mana plus cards - a one-card big turn.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are picked from the current 53-card Game Changers roster (Farewell and Biorhythm added 9 Feb 2026), filtered to this commander’s colour identity, ordered by how well they serve a defensive build-up seat, and skipping reserved-list trophies over $130. Prices are live Scryfall market prices as of 21 Aug 2026.

Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Against your stated preferences this is a double miss: it sabotages people, and it is the deck most likely to be dead before its engine matters.
Claude’s 3rd Place

Keith's favourite, and the rework earned it a podium spot: Necroskitter and Hapatra now compound every counter with no infinite loop, Kulrath Knight closes the defensive hole, and Ichor Rats headlines. Third rather than higher for the same two honest reasons as before — Friendly 2, because taking creatures is still taking creatures, and the slowest clock in the row.

Claude’s Runner-up

Esper Pillowfort Longevity — Oloro

Commander

Oloro, Ageless Ascetic{3}{W}{U}{B} Legendary Creature — Giant SoldierAt the beginning of your upkeep you gain 2 life — even while Oloro is in the command zone. Whenever you gain life, draw a card and each opponent loses 1.$19.92

Deck rarity — by stage

Modelled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (6337 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognise.

Precon seed

Any Esper shell + singles flexible Flexible seed ~$40 $91 total
Why this commander

Gains you life from the command zone whether you cast it or not. It is the only commander that pays you for doing nothing, which is exactly the subsidy a pillowfort deck needs while it sets up.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Ghostly Prison{2}{W}EnchantmentOpponents pay {2} per attacking creature. The fortress.$5.78
Propaganda{2}{U}EnchantmentThe second copy in blue — redundancy is what makes a pillowfort hold.$2.57
Approach of the Second Sun{6}{W}SorceryCast it twice and you simply win. The purest longevity win in Magic.$6.70
Test of Endurance{2}{W}{W}EnchantmentAt upkeep at 50+ life, you win.$8.52
Felidar Sovereign{4}{W}{W}Creature — Cat BeastAt upkeep at 40+ life, you win.$1.96
Sanguine Bond{3}{B}{B}EnchantmentConverts the passive lifegain into damage if you would rather close that way.$5.98

How it plays

This is the 'I was consistent and I was still there at the end' deck taken to its logical conclusion. Oloro pays you two life and a card every upkeep from the command zone, so you are ahead before you have played anything. Taxing enchantments make you the least efficient player to attack. You never sabotage anybody, you never swing, and somewhere around turn twelve you cast one spell twice and the game ends.

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modelled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changer$What it buys you
Rhystic Study$70Turns the table's own spells into your card draw.
Teferi's Protection$48Your whole board and life total phase out - the single best answer to a wipe, and it hits nobody else.
Smothering Tithe$62Every opponent draw either pays you or taxes them. Pure ramp, no targets.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are picked from the current 53-card Game Changers roster (Farewell and Biorhythm added 9 Feb 2026), filtered to this commander’s colour identity, ordered by how well they serve a defensive build-up seat, and skipping reserved-list trophies over $130. Prices are live Scryfall market prices as of 21 Aug 2026.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Two honest flags: Oloro is a Giant Soldier, the most humanlike commander in the matrix, and a pure pillowfort can read as unfun for opponents who want to attack something.
Claude’s Runner-up

The purest expression of your 'chess-like, still standing in the final two' line. Oloro pays you two life and a card every upkeep from the command zone, so you are ahead before you cast anything, and it wins without ever attacking. It scores 64% assembly and 5/5 on Longevity, Fortress and Friendly. Second because the clock is deliberately 1/5 — this deck cannot close, it can only outlast, and a hard pillowfort can read as unfun for opponents who came to attack something.

Profile-tuned · Deck 3
Claude’s 4th Place

Simic Landfall Longevity — Aesi

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Aesi, Tyrant of Gyre Strait{4}{G}{U} Legendary Creature — SerpentWhenever you play a land, draw a card. You may play an additional land each turn.$11.10

Deck rarity — by stage

Base64%Fairly familiar
Tuned70%Uncommon
Maxed74%Uncommon

Modelled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (835 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognise.

Precon seed

Any Simic ramp shell + singles flexible Flexible seed ~$40 $63 total
Why this commander

An extra land drop plus a card every time you play a land. It converts the single most reliable action in Magic into a repeatable draw engine with no setup at all.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Tatyova, Benthic Druid{3}{G}{U}Legendary Creature — Merfolk DruidSecond copy of the draw-on-landfall effect, in the 99.$0.27
Kruphix, God of Horizons{3}{G}{U}Legendary Enchantment Creature — GodUnused mana carries over as colourless. Turns patience into a stockpile.$4.26
Wall of Blossoms{1}{G}Creature — Plant WallDefensive body that replaces itself.$0.26
Lotus Cobra{1}{G}Creature — SnakeLandfall: every land is a ritual. With Aesi's extra drop, two free mana a turn.$6.17
Rampaging Baloths{4}{G}{G}Creature — BeastLandfall: a 4/4 Beast per land — two a turn with Aesi. Inevitability with no splash required.$0.33
Growth Spiral{G}{U}InstantTwo mana at instant speed: a card and an extra land onto the battlefield. Aesi a turn early.$0.30
Explore{1}{G}SorcerySame effect at sorcery speed. Two copies of the accelerator the six-mana commander needed.$0.23

How it plays

Where Obuun converts lands into bodies, Aesi converts lands into cards — which is the more chess-like version of the same idea. You defend with cheap walls, bank mana with Kruphix, and every land drop refills your hand. The convergence turn is Kruphix unbanking a stockpiled mana pool into one enormous X-spell — or simply the fourth and fifth free Baloth hitting the table.

  • Longevity: the highest in the lineup — you are structurally incapable of running out of cards.
  • Fortress: blue lets you actually protect the build with counterspells, unlike the Naya original.
  • Friendly: you interact with your own deck almost exclusively.

Room to grow — what this framework supports later

Headroom34 cards
Upgrade value~$15 ea

The two dot rows score 34 cards costing about $513 in total — roughly $15 a card, or 6.6 upgrades per $100. That total is the 7 upgrades listed above, plus about 24 more archetype-specific cards on the advanced ladder (~$400), plus the three Game Changers below (~$101). Headroom is how long that whole ladder is; Upgrade value is how cheaply it climbs.

The next cards you would buy

  • Scute Swarm
  • Ancient Greenwarden
  • Rites of Flourishing
  • Exploration

Where it sits on the Bracket 2 – 3 line

Bracket 2
Core2.61Bracket 3
Upgraded
Upper Bracket 2 · 0 of 3 Game Changers used

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modelled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
Route to the top of Bracket 3 — three colour-legal Game Changers, about $101
Game Changer$What it buys you
Field of the Dead$28A land that quietly builds an army - pure build-up.
Crop Rotation$3Turns any land into the one land that matters.
Rhystic Study$70Turns the table's own spells into your card draw.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are picked from the current 53-card Game Changers roster (Farewell and Biorhythm added 9 Feb 2026), filtered to this commander’s colour identity, ordered by how well they serve a defensive build-up seat, and skipping reserved-list trophies over $130. Prices are live Scryfall market prices as of 21 Aug 2026.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Only two colours of removal, so you rely on counterspells and blockers rather than answers after the fact.
Claude’s 4th Place

Fourth, now with its one honest knock — a six-mana commander in a deck that did nothing to get there faster — directly patched: Growth Spiral and Explore put Aesi down a turn early while feeding the landfall engine. It stays behind 3o on trust: Keith signed the Obuun build, and this one's payoffs still arrive a turn later than Gitrog's or Sythis's.

Commander

Precon seed

Any Selesnya enchantment shell + singles flexible Flexible seed ~$35 $58 total
Why this commander

Two mana for a draw engine that triggers on the permanent type your deck is already made of. Enchantments do not die to creature removal, so the engine keeps running straight through a wipe.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Sigil of the Empty Throne{3}{W}{W}EnchantmentEvery enchantment you cast makes a 4/4 Angel. The convergence payoff.$0.51
Archon of Sun's Grace{3}{W}Creature — ArchonFlying lifelink body that makes a Pegasus per enchantment.$0.65
Setessan Champion{2}{G}Creature — Human WarriorGrows and draws on every enchantment.$4.37
Eidolon of Blossoms{2}{G}{G}Enchantment Creature — SpiritAnother draw engine that is itself an enchantment.$3.32
Test of Endurance{2}{W}{W}EnchantmentAt upkeep, if you're at 50+ life, you win. A quiet alternate route.$8.52

How it plays

The most under-the-radar deck here. You spend the game laying down harmless-looking enchantments and drawing cards off each one — no board presence to threaten anybody, nothing worth removing. Then Sigil of the Empty Throne lands and every subsequent enchantment is a 4/4 Angel, and the pile of unrelated permanents you built becomes an army in two turns.

Teferi's Protection$48Your whole board and life total phase out - the single best answer to a wipe, and it hits nobody else.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. Claude’s Runner-up

The most wipe-proof deck in the matrix. Your entire engine is enchantments, so the board wipes that punish everyone else do nothing to you, and Sigil of the Empty Throne retroactively converts twenty harmless-looking permanents into an angel army. 5/5 on Rate, Card Advantage and Resilience. Second only because a two-mana commander drawing cards is less individually powerful than a 6/6 deathtouch engine, and Selesnya's interaction is thin.

Claude’s Choice

Bant Walls — Arcades

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Arcades, the Strategist{1}{G}{W}{U} Legendary Creature — Elder DragonCreatures with defender assign combat damage by toughness and can attack. Each defender you play draws a card.$4.96

Deck rarity — by stage

Base84%Rarely seen
Tuned87%Rarely seen

Modelled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (5805 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognise.

Precon seed

Any Bant shell + singles flexible Flexible seed ~$35 $42 total
Why this commander

Turns the least threatening card type in the game into a card-drawing army. Every wall you cast draws a card and swings for its toughness — defence that pays for itself twice.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Wall of Omens{1}{W}Creature — WallDraws on ETB, then draws again off Arcades. Two cards per wall.$0.31
Wall of Blossoms{1}{G}Creature — Plant WallSame trick in green.$0.26
Axebane Guardian{2}{G}Creature — Human DruidTaps for mana equal to your defender count — walls become ramp.$0.28
High Alert{1}{W}{U}EnchantmentBackup copy of the Arcades effect that survives creature wipes.$0.39
Assault Formation{1}{G}EnchantmentThird copy of the effect.$0.36
Unbreakable Formation{2}{W}InstantWipe insurance.$1.42

How it plays

The purest version of your stated playstyle in the whole matrix. Turns one through five you are playing two-mana walls that each draw a card — you look completely passive, you are drawing more cards than anybody, and no rush deck can profitably attack you. Your walls also tap for mana. Then Arcades lands, and eight defenders that everyone had mentally filed as 'nothing' simultaneously become attackers hitting for 5, 6, 7 apiece. Blue also gives you the counterspells to protect the turn it matters.

  • Convergence: a board of harmless permanents converting to lethal in one card is exactly the effect you described.
  • Friendly: you never touch anyone's board — you simply cannot be attacked.

The two dot rows score 27 cards costing about $321 in total — roughly $12 a card, or 8.4 upgrades per $100. That total is the 6 upgrades listed above, plus about 18 more archetype-specific cards on the advanced ladder (~$180), plus the three Game Changers below (~$138). Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modelled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
Route to the top of Bracket 3 — three colour-legal Game Changers, about $138
Game Changer$What it buys you
Aura Shards$29Every creature you land becomes free artifact/enchantment removal.
Teferi's Protection$48Your whole board and life total phase out - the single best answer to a wipe, and it hits nobody else.
Smothering Tithe$62Every opponent draw either pays you or taxes them. Pure ramp, no targets.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are picked from the current 53-card Game Changers roster (Farewell and Biorhythm added 9 Feb 2026), filtered to this commander’s colour identity, ordered by how well they serve a defensive build-up seat, and skipping reserved-list trophies over $130. Prices are live Scryfall market prices as of 21 Aug 2026.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Arcades is typed Elder Dragon, which brushes against the Dragons deck at your table — cosmetic only, no mechanical overlap.
Claude’s Choice

The single closest match to your stated playstyle anywhere in these thirty. Every wall you play draws a card, so defence and card advantage are literally the same action; nobody can profitably attack a board of 0/6s; your walls even tap for mana. Then Arcades resolves and eight permanents everyone had mentally written off become attackers hitting for five to seven each. 5/5 on five of your six dimensions, 76% assembly, and blue gives you counterspells to protect the turn it matters.

A free, repeatable blink every combat, in three colours stuffed with enters-the-battlefield effects. One attack step becomes a tutor, a removal spell or a draw spell depending on what you flicker.

The same engine as the Brago option with green bolted on, which fixes the two things Azorius could not: you ramp into your top end on curve instead of stumbling, and Heroic Intervention gives you a real answer to the wipe. What Keith said

Quintorius the planeswalker as commander leads this deck to victories almost every time it is played, as a stock pre-con! Never seen anyone run Excava as commander, but I see the strategy. The Skullclamp play is strong with Excava making 1/1s. Bag of Holding is BUSTED with Quintorius, it makes a spirit every time you discard.
Good call — taken in full
  • Keith was right — and the first pass wrongly corrected him. This set has three Quintorii. The earlier revision assumed he meant Quintorius Kand (the Lost Caverns planeswalker, which is not commander-legal) and swapped in the Field Historian creature instead. The card Keith actually plays is Quintorius, History Chaser — a planeswalker from this very precon whose text says "can be your commander". Restored to the helm, with apologies to Keith.
  • History Chaser is simply the best version of the plan. Four mana. The same "cards leave your graveyard → 3/2 Spirit" trigger, plus +1: discard, draw two, mill one — a one-card engine that feeds Bag of Holding, stocks the yard AND digs — plus −4: Spirits gain double strike and vigilance. The finisher is built into the commander.
  • Bag of Holding is exactly as busted as Keith says. It was already in the buy list: every discard exiles that card from your graveyard, which is a card leaving the yard, which is a Spirit. Containment Construct and Faithless Looting add two more copies of the trigger, and the commander's own +1 feeds all of them.
  • Sevinne's Reclamation added. It returns a permanent from the graveyard (one Spirit) and copies itself when cast from the graveyard (another Spirit) — the single most efficient Quintorius trigger at this budget.
  • Skullclamp gets worse, and I am not going to pretend otherwise. Quintorius makes 3/2s, not 1/1s, so Skullclamp no longer kills them and Mentor of the Meek stops triggering. Mentor is cut; Goblin Bombardment replaces it as the sacrifice outlet and the reach.
  • Field Historian and Excava both stay in the 99 — the Spirit anthem plus a redundant second trigger, and Excava still reanimates on attack. Net cost +$3.19: $73.12 to $76.31. (The earlier note claimed −$2.09 — that math double-counted Bag of Holding, which was already being bought. Corrected.)

Claude’s 3rd Place

The Endless Harvest — Muldrotha

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Muldrotha, the Gravetide{3}{B}{G}{U} Legendary Creature — Elemental AvatarEach turn, play a land plus one artifact, creature, enchantment and planeswalker from your graveyard.$1.99

Deck rarity — by stage

Base66%Fairly familiar
Tuned71%Uncommon
Maxed75%Uncommon

Modelled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (1097 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognise.

Precon seed

Faceless Menace Commander 2019 OOP — hunt it ~$50 $160 total
Why this commander

One permanent of every type per turn, out of your own graveyard, for free. It turns the graveyard into a second hand and makes removal aimed at you close to worthless.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Sidisi, Undead Vizier{3}{B}{B}Creature — Naga ShamanETB tutor for any card. Toolbox access.$8.13
The Scarab God{3}{U}{B}Legendary Creature — GodA second reanimation track running every end step.$5.25
Grave Titan{4}{B}{B}Creature — GiantSix power across three bodies, and it rebuilds you.$0.79
Living Death{3}{B}{B}SorceryA wipe you profit from — the convergence turn.$4.01
Kokusho, the Evening Star{4}{B}{B}Legendary Creature — Dragon SpiritRestored under the full brief: dies, drains 15 across the table — and this deck replays it.$26.21
Heroic Intervention{1}{G}InstantRestored under the full brief: hexproof and indestructible for the team — the wipe answer.$15.59

How it plays

Fill the yard on purpose, land Muldrotha, then play two or three extra cards a turn forever. The most decision-dense deck of the six.

  • Longevity: excellent.
  • Fortress: the gap — it does very little before turn five or six.

What Keith said

Seems good, playing out of graveyard will be fun.
Endorsed as-is — nothing changed
  • Nothing changed, on purpose. Keith had no criticism of this one, so inventing a swap to justify the label would be dishonest. This is the build exactly as it stood, carrying his sign-off.
  • What he is endorsing is the thing this deck does that no other deck in the lineup does: four independent recursion engines running at once, so removal aimed at you mostly does not matter.
  • One addition under the full $165 Capstone brief. Kokusho, the Evening Star ($26.21) and Heroic Intervention ($15.59) — the two cards the earlier sub-$10 pricing rule stripped out — are restored. Kokusho is a 15-life swing across the table that Muldrotha and The Scarab God can replay; Heroic Intervention is the answer to the board wipe this deck otherwise just absorbs. $118.18 to $159.98.
  • The one caution still stands. A single Rest in Peace or Leyline of the Void turns eight of these cards off. If someone at the table runs graveyard hate, this is the deck that feels it.

Upgrade value~$17 ea

That total is the 6 upgrades listed above, plus about 26 more archetype-specific cards on the advanced ladder (~$450), plus the three Game Changers below (~$91). Headroom is how long that whole ladder is; Upgrade value is how cheaply it climbs.

Bracket 2 (“Core”) allows no Game Changers and no two-card infinite combos, and expects games to be satisfying from turn 8. Bracket 3 (“Upgraded”) allows up to three Game Changers, with combos only as a late finish, and expects games from turn 6. Tutor limits were removed from Brackets 1–3 in the October 2025 revision, so tutors do not move this number. The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modelled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Game Changers in this build
  • None — this build is Game-Changer-free, which is what keeps it inside Bracket 2.
Route to the top of Bracket 3 — three colour-legal Game Changers, about $91
Game Changer$What it buys you
Crop Rotation$3Turns any land into the one land that matters.
Rhystic Study$70Turns the table's own spells into your card draw.
Seedborn Muse$17Untap on every turn - defence on their turns, development on yours.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. These are picked from the current 53-card Game Changers roster (Farewell and Biorhythm added 9 Feb 2026), filtered to this commander’s colour identity, ordered by how well they serve a defensive build-up seat, and skipping reserved-list trophies over $130. Prices are live Scryfall market prices as of 21 Aug 2026.

Assembly is computed, not judged: hypergeometric odds across a 99-card library that the engine's required pieces are in hand or in play by turn 8 (7 opening cards + 8 draws + this deck's own draw output), then reduced by a disruption haircut for normal opponent removal. Commander-driven engines count the command zone as always available. The other five axes are scored against how the card actually performs in this shell, not in the abstract.

Honest caveat: Strong as built. Its two real risks are graveyard hate and dying before turn six.
Claude’s 3rd Place

Third, upgraded: Kokusho and Heroic Intervention — the two cards the sub-$10 rule stripped — are restored under the full $165 brief, taking it to $160. Four recursion engines and 5/5 Longevity stand. It stays third because eight cards still fold to one Rest in Peace and it does little before turn five; the gap to the two above is now smaller than it was.

Profile-tuned · Deck 6
Claude’s Runner-up

Abzan Mass Reanimation — Nethroi

Commander

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Nethroi, Apex of Death{3}{W}{B}{G} Legendary Creature — Cat Nightmare BeastMutate. When it mutates, return creatures with total power 10 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield.$2.70

Deck rarity — by stage

Base83%Rarely seen
Tuned87%Rarely seen
Maxed89%Rarely seen

Modelled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (5451 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognise.

Precon seed

Any Abzan shell + singles flexible Flexible seed ~$40 $127 total
Why this commander

Mutate returns ten power of creatures from the yard at once. Not a reanimation spell — a reanimation event, capable of ending a game from an empty board.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Wall of Blossoms{1}{G}Creature — Plant WallCheap defence that replaces itself and later becomes reanimation fuel.$0.26
Sun Titan{4}{W}{W}Creature — GiantA second, repeatable recursion engine.$0.38
Unbreakable Formation{2}{W}InstantProtects the turn you go off.$1.42
Vindicate{1}{W}{B}SorceryAnswers the one dangerous permanent, early and cleanly.$0.67
Living Death{3}{B}{B}SorceryThe other mass-return button.$4.01
Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite{5}{W}{W}Legendary Creature — Phyrexian PraetorYour team +2/+2, theirs -2/-2 — and at power 4 she comes back under Nethroi's ten-power cap.$20.14
Craterhoof Behemoth{5}{G}{G}{G}Creature — BeastThe mutate turn returns the board; Craterhoof turns the board into the win.$23.77
Archon of Cruelty{6}{B}{B}Creature — ArchonEvery arrival drains, discards and kills. The premium reanimation target.$8.08
Vigor{3}{G}{G}{G}Creature — IncarnationDamage to your creatures becomes +1/+1 counters — a fortress in card form, and it wants to be in the yard.$12.21
Animate Dead{1}{B}Enchantment — AuraTwo mana: any creature out of the yard while you wait for the mutate.$7.56
Genesis{4}{G}{G}Creature — IncarnationFrom the graveyard, three mana a turn returns a creature to hand. Recursion that never dies.$8.67
Buried Alive{2}{B}SorceryPuts exactly the right three creatures in the yard — the mutate becomes surgical.$1.50
Fauna Shaman{1}{G}Creature — Elf ShamanRepeatable: trade a spare creature for the perfect one, stocking the yard as you go.$3.89
Luminous Broodmoth{2}{W}{W}Creature — InsectYour whole board comes back with flying counters — a wipe stops being a reset.$1.61
Karmic Guide{3}{W}{W}Creature — Angel SpiritReanimates on arrival, then gets reanimated later. Chain link.$0.39
Ashen Rider{4}{W}{W}{B}{B}Creature — ArchonExiles a permanent coming AND going — clean answers stapled to a reanimation target.$0.60

How it plays

A slower, friendlier Muldrotha. You block, you trade, your graveyard fills with creatures nobody is paying attention to — and none of it looks like a threat. Then one Nethroi mutate returns ten power of bodies at once, and the board goes from empty to lethal between one turn and the next. Abzan also means you can answer the growing threat early with Vindicate rather than waiting and making it personal.

Simic Big-Mana Convergence — Kruphix

Commander

Kruphix, God of Horizons{3}{G}{U} Legendary Enchantment Creature — GodYou have no maximum hand size. Unused mana becomes colourless instead of emptying.$4.26

Deck rarity — by stage

Base82%Rarely seen
Tuned86%Rarely seen

Modelled odds that a given opponent has not met this commander and build before. Input is the commander's live EDHREC play rank (4687 of ~30,000 tracked cards) on a log familiarity curve, bumped up if it is a precon face commander, then reduced by how far this upgrade package moves the deck off any list someone might already recognise.

Precon seed

Any Simic ramp shell + singles flexible Flexible seed ~$35 $141 total
Why this commander

Removes the two rules that cap a green deck: mana empties at end of turn, and hand size is seven. Unspent ramp becomes a stockpile instead of waste.

Key upgrades

CardCostTypeWhat it does$
Nyxbloom Ancient{4}{G}{G}{G}Enchantment Creature — ElementalTriples all your mana. The convergence trigger.$26.34
Aesi, Tyrant of Gyre Strait{4}{G}{U}Legendary Creature — SerpentExtra land drops and a card each — in the 99 here.$11.10
Wall of Blossoms{1}{G}Creature — Plant WallCheap defence while you bank.$0.26
Deepglow Skate{4}{U}Creature — FishDoubles counters on anything you've been growing.$0.29
Kruphix's Insight{2}{G}SorceryRefills your hand with enchantments — and you have no hand limit.~$1
Finale of Devastation{X}{G}{G}SorceryThe guaranteed payoff: tutor any creature straight to play, and at X=10 the whole board swings +10 with haste. The stockpile finally has a destination.$45.19
Selvala, Heart of the Wilds{1}{G}{G}Legendary Creature — Elf ScoutTaps for mana equal to the biggest power on the board, and pays you cards for big creatures. Bank faster.$5.44
Hullbreaker Horror{5}{U}{U}Creature — KrakenUncounterable flash 7/8 that bounces a spell or permanent every time you cast anything — the fortress that ends the game.$6.26
Uro, Titan of Nature's Wrath{1}{G}{U}Legendary Creature — Elder GiantRamp, draw and lifegain on every cast and escape — the early game this deck was missing.$3.17
Mana Reflection{4}{G}{G}EnchantmentEvery permanent taps for double. Stacks multiplicatively with Nyxbloom for six-times mana.$2.49
Genesis Wave{X}{G}{G}{G}SorceryThe other convergence button: put the top ten-plus permanents straight onto the battlefield.$0.44

How it plays

The most chess-like deck in the matrix. Kruphix is indestructible as long as your devotion holds, so your commander survives everything, and every turn you don't spend mana you are still getting richer. You hold a huge hand behind cheap walls while three opponents fight each other, and at the moment you choose, a tripled mana pool casts four things in one turn and the game ends. Nothing you do before that turn threatens anyone.

The position above is scored from effect-per-mana, clock, interaction density, card advantage, resilience, the modelled turn-8 assembly odds and total spend.

Three is the ceiling: a fourth would put the deck in Bracket 4. Honest caveat: The old flaw — no payoff in hand, stockpile does nothing — is now paid off directly: Finale of Devastation tutors the finisher into play, so the big turn is guaranteed rather than hoped for. Nyxbloom and Mana Reflection together are the mana linchpins; protect them.
Claude’s 4th Place

The budget pass fixed its one structural flaw: Finale of Devastation tutors the finisher straight into play, so the stockpile is no longer a bluff. Fourth because until that single big turn it threatens nothing and answers little — the most passive fortress in the row, brilliant when it lands, absent when it doesn't.

You choose exactly how much of your library goes to the graveyard and exactly which creature you keep. Almost no commander lets you tune the size of your own graveyard on cast.

The single most convergent deck in the matrix, and unusually it removes the luck from convergence. Most graveyard decks hope the right cards get milled; Stickfingers lets you pay X and deliberately stock exactly as many creatures as you want. You spend the game looking like you are doing nothing — a small frog-thing and a pile of dead cards — and then one Living Death turns twenty turns of quiet setup into a full board in a single cast.

How it plays

The most elegant capstone. Yarok reads as a modest rules change and quietly doubles the entire deck — every value creature you already wanted to play becomes twice the card. Deathtouch and lifelink on a 3/5 body means the aggressive decks leave you alone while it happens. Where Muldrotha grinds by replaying things, Yarok compounds by making each play worth double, which is a cleaner and much less hate-vulnerable version of the same 'more resources than the table' plan.
